title: How each pattern did on NSE, 2005–2026

tiers.same: No better than a plain breakout

findings: Every pattern was found with the same rules on every liquid NSE stock from 2005 to 2026, buying at the next day's open, and compared with plain breakouts: a close at a 60-day high, from the same distance below the 6-month high, in the same years.

Only the VCP beat a plain breakout: +5.0 points over the next 3 months (likely range +2.0 to +8.2), beating the average stock 65% of the time against 46%, and ahead in each period (2005–12, 2013–19, 2020–26). Bases of 6 weeks or longer did clearly better than shorter ones.
The VCP's edge shows up when the stock is held for about 3 months. With a tight −8% stop and a +20% target it won about as often as a plain breakout (32% against 30%).

This strict VCP is rare: 118 cases in 22 years, 64 of them since 2020. The simpler VCP scan in the Scanners tab fires far more often and showed a small edge: +1.7 points over plain breakouts (likely +1.3 to +2.2) across 26,045 cases.

The other patterns did about as well as a plain breakout. Bulkowski's US figures (fail 4–16%, average rise 45–55%) did not carry over: on NSE these patterns failed to move 5% in 14–25% of cases and rose 29–40% on average — about the same as plain breakouts from the same depth (18–21% and 32–39%).

Head-and-shoulders tops: the stock lagged the average stock over the next 3 months 56% of the time, about the same as on any random day (55%). Treat it as a warning to check a holding, not a proven sell signal.
method: Liquid stocks only (median turnover ₹1 Cr+ a day, price ₹10+), split- and bonus-adjusted EOD data, no look-ahead (each signal re-checked with the history cut at its day). 3-month gain is the stock's return minus the average liquid stock's, compared with matched plain breakouts; the likely range is the middle 95% of 3,000 resamples by month. Fails to move 5% and Average move follow Bulkowski: the highest price before a 20% drop. Looked right by eye: 12 random signals from 2005–19 checked on the chart.
caveats: Stocks delisted more than a year ago are missing from the data, which flatters every result a little. Eve & Eve (30 cases) and cup with handle (57) are too rare to judge. Patterns overlap: 5–32% of signals sit within a week of another pattern on the same stock.

vcp.name: VCP (volatility contraction)
vcp.about: Mark Minervini's volatility contraction pattern. A stock already in a strong uptrend pauses, and each pullback inside the pause is shallower than the one before (for example 16%, then 9%, then 5%) while volume dries up. The shrinking swings show sellers running out. The buy point is a close above the high of the last, tightest pullback.
rules: Strong uptrend first: Minervini's trend template (price above a rising 200-day average, 150-day above the 200-day, 50-day above both, at least 30% above the 52-week low and within 25% of the high) and RS rating 70+
Base of 6 to 65 weeks that starts at a peak: no higher high in the 10 sessions before it, and the top held for a few sessions (not a one-day spike)
2 to 6 pullbacks, each shallower than the one before: the first 10–40% deep, the last under 10%
Every pullback lasts a week or longer, and each low is higher than the one before
Volume during the last pullback below its 50-day average
Breakout: the first close above the high of the last pullback
vcp.levels: Stop: the low of the last pullback. No measured target: Minervini sells into strength or trails a stop.
vcp.src: Mark Minervini, Trade Like a Stock Market Wizard (2013), chapter 10

scallop.name: Inverted descending scallop
scallop.about: An upside-down J. Price rises from A to a rounded top at B, then slides in a curve to C, below where it started. A close back above B says the selling that followed the top is over.
rules: A rise from A to B, then a rounded slide to C that ends below A (the rise is 30–85% of the slide)
A rounded top, not a spike: a quarter or more of the bars sit near the top, and the closes follow an arc
3 to 40 weeks from A to C; the slide from B to C is at least 10%
Breakout: the first close above B, before price falls below C
scallop.levels: Stop: the low at C. Target: B plus the height from C to B.
scallop.src: Thomas Bulkowski, Encyclopedia of Chart Patterns (3rd ed.) and thepatternsite.com

ihs.name: Inverse head and shoulders
ihs.about: Three lows after a decline. The middle low (the head) is the deepest; the two shoulders on either side sit at about the same level. The line across the two rally highs is the neckline, and a close above it confirms the bottom.
rules: Price falls into the pattern: the 3-month high before it is at least half a pattern height above the neckline
Head at least 20% of the pattern height below the higher shoulder; the shoulders within 20% of the height of each other
Each shoulder a real dip (30–85% as deep as the head); the right side takes 0.5 to 2 times as long as the left
4 to 50 weeks from shoulder to shoulder; height at least 10%; neckline tilt at most 40% of the height; closes follow the shape
Breakout: the first close above the neckline (above the right rally high when the neckline slopes up), before price undercuts the head
ihs.levels: Stop: the right shoulder's low. Target: the neckline plus the pattern's height.
ihs.src: Thomas Bulkowski, Encyclopedia of Chart Patterns (3rd ed.) and thepatternsite.com

bigw.name: Big W
bigw.about: A double bottom with a tall, straight fall on its left. Price drops steeply, makes two lows close together, and a close above the rally high between the lows completes the W.
rules: Two lows within 6% of each other, 2 to 12 weeks apart, with a rally of at least 10% between them
The fall into the first low is at least twice the pattern's height, nearly straight, and 3 to 25 weeks long; the first low is the bottom of that fall
Height at least 12%
Breakout: the first close above the rally high between the two lows
bigw.levels: Stop: the lower of the two lows. Target: the breakout level plus the pattern's height.
bigw.src: Thomas Bulkowski, Encyclopedia of Chart Patterns (3rd ed.) and thepatternsite.com

tb.name: Triple bottom
tb.about: Three lows at about the same price, separated by two rallies. Buyers step in at the same level three times; a close above the higher of the two rally highs confirms it.
rules: Three lows within 5% of each other (and within a quarter of the pattern's height)
Each rally between them at least 40% of the height; lows at least 8 sessions apart and all within a year
Price falls into it; no low more than 2% below the first; height at least 10%
Breakout: the first close above the highest rally high
tb.levels: Stop: the lowest of the three lows. Target: the breakout level plus the pattern's height.
tb.src: Thomas Bulkowski, Encyclopedia of Chart Patterns (3rd ed.) and thepatternsite.com

rectb.name: Rectangle bottom
rectb.about: After a decline, price moves sideways between two flat lines: a ceiling it touches again and again, and a floor it keeps holding. A close above the ceiling is the upward breakout.
rules: Price fell into the box: the high of the 3 months before is at least half a box height above it
4 to 50 weeks long and 5–20% tall; at least 3 touches of one line and 2 of the other, in both halves of the box
Flat: the closes drift by no more than a quarter of the box height from one end to the other
Breakout: a close above the ceiling that is also a 20-day high
rectb.levels: Stop: the floor. Target: the ceiling plus the box height.
rectb.src: Thomas Bulkowski, Encyclopedia of Chart Patterns (3rd ed.) and thepatternsite.com

chs.name: Complex head and shoulders bottom
chs.about: An inverse head and shoulders with extra parts: two heads side by side, or two or more shoulders on one side. A close above the neckline joining the highest rally points confirms it.
rules: Four or five lows after a decline: a head (one or two lows at the bottom) in the middle, shoulders on both sides
Head at least 20% of the height below the shoulders; the outer shoulders within 25% of the height of each other
5 to 50 weeks; height at least 10%; neckline tilt at most 40% of the height
Breakout: the first close above the neckline, within 4 weeks of the last shoulder
chs.levels: Stop: the head's low. Target: the neckline plus the pattern's height.
chs.src: Thomas Bulkowski, Encyclopedia of Chart Patterns (3rd ed.) and thepatternsite.com

3rv.name: Three rising valleys
3rv.about: Three dips, each bottoming at least 2% higher than the one before, like steps. Rising lows show buyers paying more each time; the signal is a close above the highest peak between them.
rules: Each low at least 2% above the one before
Valleys of similar width; each rally between them at least 30% of the height
At least 6 sessions between lows, all within 40 weeks; height at least 8%
Breakout: the first close above the highest peak
3rv.levels: Stop: the first (lowest) valley. Target: the breakout level plus the pattern's height.
3rv.src: Thomas Bulkowski, Encyclopedia of Chart Patterns (3rd ed.) and thepatternsite.com

rectt.name: Rectangle top
rectt.about: After a rise, price pauses between two flat lines: a ceiling it touches again and again, and a floor it keeps holding. A close above the ceiling continues the uptrend.
rules: Price rose into the box: the low of the 3 months before is at least half a box height below it
4 to 50 weeks long and 5–20% tall; at least 3 touches of one line and 2 of the other, in both halves of the box
Flat: the closes drift by no more than a quarter of the box height from one end to the other
Breakout: a close above the ceiling that is also a 20-day high
rectt.levels: Stop: the floor. Target: the ceiling plus the box height.
rectt.src: Thomas Bulkowski, Encyclopedia of Chart Patterns (3rd ed.) and thepatternsite.com

rb.name: Rounding bottom
rb.about: A slow, bowl-shaped turn: price declines gradually, flattens out, and climbs back just as gradually. A close above the bowl's left rim completes it.
rules: A bowl 8 to 65 weeks wide and 12–60% deep
The closes follow a smooth U, checked against an ideal curve; the low sits in the middle 60% of the bowl
The left rim is a real peak, and the bottom is wide, not a spike
Breakout: the first close above the left rim (also a 20-day high)
rb.levels: Stop: the bowl's low. Target: the rim plus the bowl's depth.
rb.src: Thomas Bulkowski, Encyclopedia of Chart Patterns (3rd ed.) and thepatternsite.com

barr.name: Bump-and-run reversal bottom
barr.about: A gentle decline along a falling trendline (the lead-in), then a sudden, steep plunge (the bump) as selling turns to panic, then a recovery that closes back above the trendline.
rules: Lead-in: a falling trendline through two swing highs, for at least a quarter of the pattern
The bump drops at least 2.5 times as far below the line as the lead-in did, and falls at least 2.5 times as steeply
8 to 60 weeks long; the bump at least 15% deep
Breakout: the first close above the trendline, 5 or more sessions after the bump's low
barr.levels: Stop: the bump's low. Target: the breakout level plus the bump's depth.
barr.src: Thomas Bulkowski, Encyclopedia of Chart Patterns (3rd ed.) and thepatternsite.com

ee.name: Eve & Eve double bottom
ee.about: Two wide, rounded lows at about the same price. Bulkowski calls a wide, rounded bottom an Eve and a narrow spike an Adam. A close above the rally high between them confirms the double bottom.
rules: Two lows within 6% of each other, 2 to 12 weeks apart, with a rally of at least 10% between them
Both lows wide and rounded: 8 or more sessions near each low
It follows a decline: the 3-month high before the first low is at least one pattern height above the breakout
Height at least 12%; breakout: the first close above the rally high between the lows
ee.levels: Stop: the lower of the two lows. Target: the breakout level plus the pattern's height.
ee.src: Thomas Bulkowski, Encyclopedia of Chart Patterns (3rd ed.) and thepatternsite.com

cwh.name: Cup with handle
cwh.about: William O'Neil's base. A rounded, U-shaped cup 7 to 65 weeks long, then a short, shallow pullback near the top (the handle). The buy point is a close above the handle's high on strong volume.
rules: A prior uptrend of 30% or more; the cup's left rim within 5% of the 6-month high and not a one-day spike
Cup 12–35% deep and U-shaped (the closes follow a U); its two rims within −7% to +3% of each other
Handle 1 to 12 weeks, 2–12% deep, in the upper half of the cup, drifting sideways or down, on volume no more than 1.1 times the 50-day average
Breakout: the first close above the handle's high, on volume at least 1.4 times the 50-day average
cwh.levels: Stop: the handle's low. Target: the breakout level plus the cup's depth.
cwh.src: William O'Neil, How to Make Money in Stocks; Thomas Bulkowski, Encyclopedia of Chart Patterns (3rd ed.) and thepatternsite.com

hst.name: Head and shoulders top
hst.about: The mirror image of the inverse head and shoulders, at the end of a rise: three peaks, the middle one (the head) the highest. A close below the neckline across the two dips is the classic sell signal.
rules: Price rises into the pattern: the 3-month low before it is at least half a pattern height below the neckline
Head at least 20% of the height above the higher shoulder; the shoulders within 20% of the height of each other
4 to 50 weeks from shoulder to shoulder; height at least 10%; neckline tilt at most 40% of the height
Breakdown: the first close below the neckline, before price goes above the head
hst.levels: The neckline is the level to watch. Bulkowski's target: the neckline minus the pattern's height.
hst.src: Thomas Bulkowski, Encyclopedia of Chart Patterns (3rd ed.) and thepatternsite.com
